name: ACh encode/retrieve gate
interface: I1 encode-vs-retrieve mode of fast store
mechanism: Acetylcholine sets hippocampal encode-vs-retrieve dynamics: high ACh (novelty/waking) suppresses CA3->CA1 recurrent retrieval and favours feedforward encoding of new patterns; low ACh (SWS) releases retrieval for consolidation. EXACTLY the H_1532 'phase-1 A->B written with retrieval-path SUPPRESSED = Hasselmo encode-mode' primitive.
citation: Hasselmo 2006 Trends Cogn Sci 10(11):522; Hasselmo & McGaughy 2004
needs_two_store_why: On a flat store there is no fast buffer to put in encode-mode without losing retrieval entirely (H_1532 DECONFOUND: encode-mode alone in one store = 0.292). ACh gates which store-mode the fast store is in while the slow store keeps recall available — only separable with two stores.
frozen_bar_sketch: Capability = AB-AC interference with graded novelty (surprise=fast-store recon-err). ARMS: A fixed encode-mode two-store / B ACh-gated encode (engage encode-mode proportional to surprise) / ABL ACh->constant / SHUFFLE ACh permuted. GREEN iff B-A>=+0.10 on >=2/3 seeds AND ABL reverts AND SHUFFLE collapses.
cheapest_refuter: single-store+ACh-graded-encode arm: if it matches two-store+ACh, ACh is a gain not an interface (H_1422 ACh-gain wall). Plus the merge ablation. RISK: scalar-on-threshold re-enters the controller family.
wires_into: core/engine_cli.hexa ConsolidatingMemory novelty-split surprise=recon-err (H_1285, exists); H_1532 fast-episodic encode-mode write
status_note: being implemented as H_1541; GREEN hinges on beating single-store+ACh DECONFOUND not just two-store-fixed

name: DA replay-priority (prioritized consolidation)
mechanism: Dopamine tags which episodes consolidate first: VTA-hippocampal loop gates replay salience; computationally = prioritized replay (replay highest expected value-of-backup first). H_1536 DA-RPE (GREEN) ALREADY produces the priority: per-identity learned value V(s)=credit a stored fact carries.
citation: Mattar & Daw 2018 Nat Neurosci 21:1609; Lisman-Grace 2005; McNamara et al 2014 Nat Neurosci
needs_two_store_why: Prioritized replay is a transfer-ordering over the fast->slow channel; on a flat store there is no transfer to order. The slow store is the target of the priority; remove it and 'which to replay first' is undefined. Standalone DA-RPE assigns credit; inside CLS it routes consolidation bandwidth under a budget = a DIFFERENT mechanism.
frozen_bar_sketch: Capability = bounded-budget consolidation: slow store absorbs only K<N fast episodes/sweep; high-value (DA-RPE) must survive, low evicted. ARMS: A uniform replay (H_1285 arm-A) / B DA-value-priority replay / ABL DA->0=uniform / SHUFFLE value<->episode permuted. GREEN iff B.important-recall>=A+0.10 AND ABL reverts AND SHUFFLE<bar. Reuses H_1285 salience-replay harness verbatim, swap surprise-salience for DA-RPE value.
cheapest_refuter: set slow-store budget K=N (no scarcity): if DA-priority gives no lift when everything fits, the lever was the budget not DA (scopes the claim). Plus merge ablation (one store=no transfer=priority undefined).
wires_into: H_1285 consolidating_sleep_replay (salience-proportional, ALREADY GREEN WIRED) + H_1536 DA-RPE value head. Two LIVE GREEN faculties composed = highest-readiness joint candidate.
status_note: highest readiness: composes two already-GREEN live faculties

name: Sleep-stage consolidation wiring (CLS slow-store = replay phase)
mechanism: Systems consolidation: hippocampal fast store replays to neocortical slow store during slow-wave sleep. Literally the CLS slow store. anima ALREADY has the ultradian machinery (WAKE->N1->N2->N3->REM 90-tick dr_stage_at), emit-free ir_replay_session, ir_reconsolidate_session recency write-back (H_1195), and consolidating_sleep_replay salience-replay (H_1285 GREEN WIRED).
citation: Diekelmann & Born 2010 Nat Rev Neurosci 11:114; Rasch & Born 2013 Physiol Rev; McClelland-McNaughton-O'Reilly 1995
needs_two_store_why: H_1136 measured a BLOCKED-WIRING null: the sleep loop did NOT consolidate because there was no second store to write back into (post-sleep anchor state byte-identical to no-sleep, Delta=0). The CLS slow store IS the missing write-back target. N3 replay should move fast-episodic traces INTO a distinct slow store. Maps to ultradian: WAKE=encode (ACh I1), N1/N2=DA-priority candidate select (I2), N3=slow-wave consolidation sweep (fast->slow, consolidating_sleep_replay redirected to write slow store), REM=reconsolidation refresh (ir_reconsolidate_session). phi_EI peaks N3 (H_1119).
frozen_bar_sketch: Capability = early-fact retention after long interfering stream WITH interposed N3 sweep vs WITHOUT (matched wall-clock = same pure_field_step count = H_1136 no-sleep control). ARMS: A no-sleep control / B two-store+N3 fast->slow transfer / ABL N3 sweep but slow store disabled (=H_1136 BLOCKED-WIRING null, Delta=0 expected, PRE-VALIDATED) / SHUFFLE replay random episodes. GREEN iff B.retention-A>=+0.10 AND ABL~0 AND SHUFFLE<bar.
cheapest_refuter: the H_1136 no-sleep wall-clock control IS the refuter, ALREADY BUILT in h1136_sleep_consolidation_probe.hexa: if B does not exceed matched no-sleep by the bar, slow-store consolidation adds nothing over chronological aging. CHEAPEST refuter in the census (harness exists).
wires_into: DREAM/imagination_replay (ir_replay_session, ir_reconsolidate_session, ir_mitosis_tick_during_replay), DREAM/dream_lib (dr_stage_at), core/engine_cli.hexa ConsolidatingMemory (consolidating_sleep_replay), a_chat_sleep_imagination. slow store = 2nd ConsolidatingMemory instance the N3 sweep writes into.
status_note: STRONGEST NEAR-FREE STRUCTURAL FIT: every live piece exists, control pre-built+pre-validated, closes the H_1136 measured open gap

name: NE context-boundary fast-store flush (reopen H_1537)
mechanism: NE phasic burst = network reset at an event/context boundary that abandons the stale model. H_1537 walled this on a single learner (best fixed gain alpha*=0.6 itself acts as partial reset, flush adds only +0.029) but named the next lens: NONLINEAR-policy / structural-context not-ruled-out.
citation: Bouret & Sara 2005 Trends Neurosci 28:574; Yu & Dayan 2005; Zacks et al 2007 event-segmentation
needs_two_store_why: H_1537 walled because the fixed gain itself subsumes the reset - nothing structural to flush. Inside two-store there IS: the fast episodic buffer accumulates within-context bindings; at an event boundary NE flushes the FAST store (clears within-episode interference) WHILE the slow store retains consolidated cross-context knowledge. Flushing the fast store while slow persists = event-segmentation, a structural action a scalar gain cannot do (flushing the only store is catastrophic). The H_1537 single-learner scope did not cover the two-store regime.
frozen_bar_sketch: Capability = AB / context-switch / CD: write A->B (ctx1), boundary, write C->D (ctx2), query A->B must survive AND C->D must not leak into ctx1 recall. ARMS: A no-flush two-store / B NE-flush fast store at detected boundary (surprise=fast recon-err spike) / ABL flush detector OFF / SHUFFLE flush at random ticks. GREEN iff B-A>=+0.10 AND ABL reverts AND SHUFFLE collapses.
cheapest_refuter: single-store+NE-flush arm in the SAME run: H_1537 showed single-store flush ~= best-fixed-gain (+0.029 sub-bar). If two-store NE-flush does not beat single-store NE-flush, the wall HOLDS inside two-store too (stays WALL). Plus merge ablation (flush merged store=catastrophic by construction).
wires_into: H_1532 fast episodic store (flush target); core/engine_cli.hexa ConsolidatingMemory recon-err surprise (boundary detector); slow store (retained side)
status_note: a_break_the_wall REOPEN under new scope, NOT a claim the wall is wrong; single-store-flush refuter must be in the SAME run to earn the reopen

name: 5-HT replay-timing / consolidation patience
mechanism: 5-HT = patience/temporal-discounting controller of WHEN to act. Inside CLS the gated action = when to fire the consolidation sweep: too eager wastes budget replaying unstable traces; waiting lets fast-store traces mature before the expensive transfer (synaptic tagging-and-capture timing). H_1538 found patience PRESENT+EARNED (+0.1911) but fixed-gamma captures ~51% (AMBER, mechanism-attribution bar C failed).
citation: Miyazaki et al 2014 Curr Biol 24:2033; Doya 2002 Neural Networks 15:495; Frey & Morris 1997 (tagging-and-capture)
needs_two_store_why: The action 5-HT discounts is the fast->slow sweep trigger - there is no sweep to time on a single store. The patience tradeoff (wait for grounding to rise vs consolidate now) maps onto fast-store trace maturity: a young trace replayed consolidates noise, a matured trace consolidates signal.
frozen_bar_sketch: Capability = consolidation quality vs latency: slow-store recall accuracy vs sweep-trigger timing with per-tick wait cost. ARMS: A eager always-sweep / B 5-HT-patience (sweep when trace-maturity discounted-value peaks) / ABL fixed-gamma / SHUFFLE maturity<->trace permuted. GREEN iff B-A>=+0.10 AND B-ABL>=0.5*lift (the bar H_1538 FAILED standalone) AND SHUFFLE collapses.
cheapest_refuter: the fixed-gamma ABL arm (the one that gave H_1538 its AMBER): if a fixed consolidation cadence matches adaptive 5-HT timing inside two-store too, 5-HT-timing is a minority lever here as well. Honest prior: probably reproduces H_1538 AMBER.
wires_into: rank-3 N3 sweep trigger; H_1538 patience faculty; dr_stage_at cadence
status_note: AMBER-likely: fixed cadence may tie, as standalone H_1538

name: GABA E/I-balance store-capacity gating
mechanism: GABAergic inhibition sets sparsity/E-I balance controlling pattern-separation capacity and per-episode engram cell count. Inside CLS would gate the fast store's per-episode cell budget (sparse=better AB-AC separation, dense=more capacity but more interference).
citation: Stefanelli et al 2016 (engram size set by inhibition); Sahay et al 2011 (inhibition & pattern separation)
needs_two_store_why: MARGINAL: E/I sparsity is largely a single-store representation-geometry knob (H_1527 family). Only two-store-specific if inhibition gates fast vs slow sparsity DIFFERENTLY (fast=sparse for separation, slow=dense for generalization, a genuine CLS asymmetry). Without that asymmetry it re-enters the geometry family.
frozen_bar_sketch: ARMS: A symmetric sparsity / B fast-sparse/slow-dense E/I asymmetry / ABL equal sparsity / SHUFFLE sparsity-assignment permuted. GREEN iff the ASYMMETRY beats both symmetric settings.
cheapest_refuter: single-store sparsity sweep (H_1527 family): if best-fixed sparsity on one store matches the asymmetry, GABA is a geometry knob not a CLS interface (reject, likely outcome).
wires_into: core/engine_cli.hexa ConsolidatingMemory split-threshold/cell budget; H_1527 representation-geometry family
status_note: reject-likely: collapses into H_1527 geometry family unless fast/slow asymmetry is load-bearing

name: Orexin/histamine arousal-gated encode-rate
interface: I1 wake-stage encode rate / sleep transition
mechanism: Orexin/hypocretin and histamine set arousal/wake-drive and thereby the rate of new encoding vs propensity for offline consolidation (the wake-side complement to the ACh/SWS consolidation axis). Inside CLS would modulate WAKE-stage fast-store write-rate and the WAKE<->sleep transition gating the slow sweep.
needs_two_store_why: WEAK: arousal-gated encode-rate is mostly redundant with rank-1 ACh encode-gate and rank-3 sleep-stage timing - it modulates the transition into the sleep sweep, which dr_stage_at already schedules deterministically. Likely no orthogonal lever beyond ACh (I1)+sleep cadence (I3).
frozen_bar_sketch: Would have to show arousal-gated encode-rate beats the FIXED WAKE-encode schedule - but dr_stage_at is already a fixed schedule that works.
cheapest_refuter: the fixed dr_stage_at schedule itself: if a fixed wake/sleep cadence matches arousal-gated rate, orexin/histamine add nothing. Honest null candidate.
wires_into: DREAM/dream_lib dr_stage_at transition; rank-1 ACh; rank-3 sleep wiring
status_note: honest null: redundant with dr_stage_at fixed schedule + ACh encode-gate
